To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
TGF- β and c-myc mediate the regulation of PTP-1 expression by breast cancer cells to promote the integration of breast cancer cells with bone marrow stroma.
the BM stroma regulates the expression of TGF-β, which in turn regulates the expression of PTT-I in BCC.
the expression of PTT-I and TGF-b in breast cancer cells and stromal cells is influenced by the interaction of these cells with each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how BCCs interact with BM stroma to facilitate the development of breast cancer metastasis.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate BCC integration within the BM stroma.
the role of the BM stroma in the regulation of the gene for PPT-I in both BCC and BM stroma.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the BM stroma influences the expression of cytokines and the PPT-I in both BCC and stromal cells and that the cytokine TGF-β mediates the induction of PPT- I by c-myc in BCCs to facilitate the early events of BCC invasion of the BM.
TGF- β and c-myc are required for PPT-I induction in BCCs and are important to the integration of BCCs into BM stroma.
TGF- β and c-myc play a role in the expression of PTP-I in BCC integration within the BM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TGF- β and PPT-I are important in the early events in the metastasis of breast cancer to the BM.
TGF- β and c-myc are important to the expression of the PPT-1 gene in the early events that lead to bone invasion by breast cancer.
TGF- β is an important factor for the early events of metastatic breast cancer to the BM.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the microenvironmental milieu of the BM influences the production of TGF-β by both BCCs (and stroma) to regulate c-myc activation of PPT-I gene expression in BCCs.
the bone marrow stroma influences the production of TGF-β from breast cancer cells to regulate the c-myc activation of the preprotachytkinin-I gene.
TGF- β and c-myc are key mediators of PPT-I expression, which may be important to breast cancer cell invasion of the BM.
